The electromagnet produces a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the ground. When the first carriage passes over the coil placed between the two rails, the electric pulse signal produced in the coil is transmitted to the control center. Figure B shows the electric pulse signal on the display screen of the control center at a certain time. Then the train's state of motion at this time is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure A, an electromagnet is installed under the first carriage of the train. The electromagnet produces a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the ground. When the first carriage passes over the coil placed between the two rails, the electric pulse signal produced in the coil is transmitted to the control center. According to the electric pulse signal on the display screen of the control center at a certain time in Figure B, what motion is the train doing at this time?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In Figure A, below the first carriage of the train there is a “magnetic field region” marked by a dashed-line box; the two thick lines beside it indicate “rails”; a “coil” is placed between the two rails; the coil is “connected to the control center” through wires. Figure B is the u-t graph displayed by the control center; the vertical axis is labeled u/V, and the horizontal axis is labeled t/s; in the figure one positive pulse line segment slopes downward with time, and another negative pulse line segment rises upward toward zero with time, indicating that whether the pulse is positive or negative, the absolute value of the induced voltage decreases approximately linearly with time. Then reason: the electromagnet below the train produces a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the ground, and when it passes over the fixed coil, the magnetic flux of the coil changes, producing an induced voltage. For a uniform magnetic field and fixed coil geometric conditions, the magnitude of the induced voltage is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux, and the rate of change of magnetic flux is proportional to the train speed, so |u|∝v. Figure B shows that |u| decreases linearly with time; therefore the train speed decreases linearly with time, that is, the acceleration is negative and its magnitude is constant. Final answer: the train is doing uniformly decelerated motion.
